### Observed differences

- In the later window, A02 appears in about 56% of traces (mean 0.575) versus 20% before, and its average position moves from about 68% to 19% of the trace, i.e. much earlier. [OCC001, POS001]
- A27, present in every trace before, appears in only about 46% of traces after (mean 0.465). [OCC006]
- A32 and A33 are essentially absent before (0% and 0.5% participation) and appear in about 55% of traces each after. [OCC007, OCC008]
- A04, A10 and A23 decrease in participation (from about 21%, 17%, 59% to 5%, 5%, 41% respectively), while A24 increases from 42% to 60%. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005]
- A02's outgoing transitions change from a spread over many activities (A46 27%, A44 17%, A16 15%) to almost exclusively A15 (about 95%). [DIR001]
- A14's outgoing transitions change from mostly A15 (93%) to A02 (55%) and A15 (44%). [DIR003]
- A26's outgoing transitions change from mostly A27 (98%) to A27 (44%), A33 (33%) and A32 (21%). [DIR004]
- A32 and A33, absent before, now have outgoing transitions mainly to A28 and to each other. [DIR006, DIR007]
- Relationally, A14 now precedes A02 in about 54% of traces (vs 19% before), and A02 precedes A15 in about 35% (vs 1% before). [REL001, REL002]
- A27's cooccurrence with A14, A15, A26, A28, A45 and A46 drops from 100% to about 46%, with A27 absent in the remaining traces. [REL010, REL013, REL016, REL019, REL022, REL023]
- A32 and A33 appear together in about 55% of traces, with A33 before A32 in about 34% and A32 before A33 in about 21%. [REL026]
- Lags: A14 to A02 becomes immediate (lag 1 in 99% vs 25% before), A02 to A15 becomes more immediate (lag 1 in 54% vs 38% before), and A26 to A28 shifts from lag 2 (97%) to lag 3 (51%) and lag 2 (44%). [LAG002, LAG001, LAG004]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a structural change in which a new path is introduced: A14 → A02 → A15, and new activities A32 and A33 appear, often leading to A28, while A27 is skipped in about half the cases. The change is directly shown by occurrence increases/decreases, routing shifts, positional moves, and relational/lag patterns that all point to the same reorganisation. The main competing explanation—that the later window simply contains a different mix of pre-existing variants—is unlikely given the large number of indicators (56 items vs 0.72 expected by chance) and their consistency. The evidence cannot, however, reveal the cause or business meaning of the change. [OCC001, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, DIR001, DIR003, DIR004, DIR006, DIR007, REL001, REL002, REL010, REL013, REL016, REL019, REL022, REL023, REL026, LAG001, LAG002, LAG004]
